name: get_pt_information
title: Get Packet Tracer Information
description:
Connect to Cisco Packet Tracer over IPC and report its version, the IPC API spec in use,
device/link counts, workspace mode (logical/physical, realtime/simulation) and the open file.
Call this first to confirm the connection works.

Examples:
- "Is Packet Tracer connected?"
- "What version of Packet Tracer is running?"
- "How many devices are in my network?"

pt_version.description: Packet Tracer version reported over IPC (e.g. '9.0.1.0858')

ipc_api_spec.description: Bundled IPC API spec in use

logical_mode.description: True when the Logical workspace is showing

simulation_mode.description: True when in Simulation mode (False = Realtime)

file.description: Saved filename of the active network, if any

name: get_devices_in_network
title: Get All Devices in the Network
description:
List every device in the active Packet Tracer network: name, IPC class, model, device type,
power state and logical-workspace x/y position. Packet Tracer's auto-created power distribution
device is hidden unless include_infrastructure=true.

Examples:
- "What devices are in my Packet Tracer network?"
- "List all routers and switches"
- "Show me the topology"

class_name.description: IPC class (e.g. Router, CiscoDevice, Pc, Server)

annotations.title: Get All Devices in the Network

name: get_device_models
title: Get Available Device Models
description:
List the device models Packet Tracer offers for a device type. Use one of these model
strings with add_device_to_network.

Examples:
- "Which router models can I add?"
- "List the available switch models"
- "What PC models does Packet Tracer have?"

name: add_device_to_network
title: Add a Device to the Network
description:
Add a device to the logical workspace. Returns the device's name (Packet Tracer assigns one such
as 'Router0'; it is renamed to `name` if given).

Required: device_type (e.g. "router", "switch", "pc", "server"), model (e.g. "2911", "ISR4331",
"2960-24TT", "PC-PT", "Server-PT" -- discover via get_device_models).
Optional: x/y position, name.

Examples:
- "Add a 2911 router called R1"
- "Put a 2960 switch at 300,200"
- "Add two PCs to the network"

anyOf.description: Device display name as shown in Packet Tracer (e.g. 'Router0', 'PC1')

annotations.title: Add a Device to the Network

name: rename_device
title: Rename a Device
description:
Change a device's display name (the name used by all other tools). This does not change the IOS
hostname; use send_cli_command with "hostname X" for that.

Examples:
- "Rename Router0 to R1"
- "Call PC0 'Accounting-PC'"

name.description: Device display name as shown in Packet Tracer (e.g. 'Router0', 'PC1')

new_name.description: Device display name as shown in Packet Tracer (e.g. 'Router0', 'PC1')

name: set_device_power
title: Set Device Power
description:
Power a device on or off. Powering off a Cisco device discards its unsaved running-config.

Examples:
- "Turn off R1"
- "Power on all the switches"

name.description: Device display name as shown in Packet Tracer (e.g. 'Router0', 'PC1')

name: delete_device_from_network
title: Delete a Device from the Network
description:
Delete a device and all of its links from the network.

CRITICAL: Destructive and irreversible (the device's configuration is lost). Always ask
"Confirm deletion of [device]?" and wait for the user's "yes" before invoking this tool.

Examples:
- "Delete R2"
- "Remove the extra switch"

name.description: Device display name as shown in Packet Tracer (e.g. 'Router0', 'PC1')

annotations.title: Delete a Device from the Network

name: get_interfaces_for_device
title: Get Interfaces for a Device
description:
List a device's ports: name, IPC class, link/protocol state, MAC, IPv4 address/mask (host
ports), and the remote port name if a cable is attached.

Examples:
- "What interfaces does R1 have?"
- "Which ports on the switch are connected?"
- "Show PC0's IP address"

name.description: Device display name as shown in Packet Tracer (e.g. 'Router0', 'PC1')

remote_device.description: Device at the other end of the attached cable

remote_port.description: Port name at the other end of the attached cable

name: configure_host_interface
title: Configure an End-Device Interface
description:
Set IPv4 settings on an end device's port (PC, laptop, server, printer...). Typical port names:
'FastEthernet0' (PC-PT), 'GigabitEthernet0'. For routers and switches use send_cli_command.
subnet_mask defaults to 255.255.255.0 when ip_address is given. dhcp=true switches the port to DHCP.

Examples:
- "Give PC0 192.168.1.10/24 with gateway 192.168.1.1"
- "Set the server's DNS to 8.8.8.8"
- "Put PC1 on DHCP"

name.description: Device display name as shown in Packet Tracer (e.g. 'Router0', 'PC1')

name: set_interface_power
title: Set Interface Power
description:
Administratively enable or disable a port at the physical level (like plugging/unplugging the port's
power in Packet Tracer). For IOS 'shutdown'/'no shutdown' use send_cli_command.

Examples:
- "Disable PC0's FastEthernet0"

name.description: Device display name as shown in Packet Tracer (e.g. 'Router0', 'PC1')

name: connect_two_devices
title: Connect Two Devices
description:
Cable a port on one device to a port on another and return the cable type used. Both ports must
exist and be free; use get_interfaces_for_device to find port names. cable="auto" (default) picks
like Packet Tracer's GUI: serial for Serial ports, console for console ports, straight-through between
a switch and a host/router, crossover between like devices.

Examples:
- "Connect R1 Gi0/0 to SW1 Gi0/1"
- "Cable PC0 FastEthernet0 to the switch's Fa0/1"
- "Add a serial link between R1 Serial0/1/0 and R2 Serial0/1/0"

device_a.description: Device display name as shown in Packet Tracer (e.g. 'Router0', 'PC1')

device_b.description: Device display name as shown in Packet Tracer (e.g. 'Router0', 'PC1')

name: get_all_links
title: Get All Links in the Network
description:
List every cable in the network as device/port pairs with the cable type.

Examples:
- "Show all the links"
- "What is R1 connected to?"
- "Map the topology connections"

annotations.title: Get All Links in the Network

name: delete_link
title: Delete a Link
description:
Remove the cable attached to a device port.

CRITICAL: Destructive. Always ask "Confirm removal of the link on [device] [port]?" and wait for
the user's "yes" before invoking this tool.

Examples:
- "Disconnect R1 Gi0/0"
- "Remove the cable between PC0 and the switch"

device.description: Device display name as shown in Packet Tracer (e.g. 'Router0', 'PC1')

name: send_cli_command
title: Send CLI Command to a Cisco Device
description:
Send IOS commands to a Cisco device (router, switch, multilayer switch, ASA, WLC...) and return each
command's status and output. Works even before the device finishes booting (boot is skipped).

- Separate multiple commands with newlines.
- config_command=false (default): privileged exec mode (e.g. "show ip interface brief").
- config_command=true: configuration mode -- DO NOT include "enable", "configure terminal" or "end".
  Sub-modes carry over, so "interface Gi0/0\nip address 10.0.0.1 255.255.255.0\nno shutdown" works.
- status is "invalid"/"incomplete"/"ambiguous" when IOS rejected a command.

CRITICAL: Can modify device state. Review commands carefully before executing, especially when
config_command=true.

Examples:
- "Run 'show ip route' on R1"
- "Configure Gi0/0 on R1 with 10.0.0.1/24 and bring it up"
- "Show the running config of SW1"

name.description: Device display name as shown in Packet Tracer (e.g. 'Router0', 'PC1')

status.description: ok | rejected (IOS printed a '% ...' error) | ambiguous | invalid | incomplete | not_implemented

annotations.title: Send CLI Command to a Cisco Device

name: send_terminal_command
title: Send Command to an End-Device Terminal
description:
Type one command into a device's terminal and collect its output -- for PCs, laptops and servers this
is the Desktop > Command Prompt ('ping 10.0.0.1', 'ipconfig /all', 'tracert 8.8.8.8', 'arp -a').
Output is collected until Packet Tracer reports the command ended or the timeout passes; pings
in Realtime mode take a few seconds.

Examples:
- "Ping 192.168.1.1 from PC0"
- "Run ipconfig on the laptop"
- "Traceroute from PC1 to the server"

name.description: Device display name as shown in Packet Tracer (e.g. 'Router0', 'PC1')

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the command to finish

completed.description: True if Packet Tracer reported the command finished before the timeout

annotations.title: Send Command to an End-Device Terminal

name: verify_connectivity
title: Verify Connectivity (Ping Test)
description:
Ping each destination from a device (PC/server Command Prompt or a Cisco device) and report sent/received/
loss per destination. A destination that loses everything is retried (ARP resolution and STP on fresh
switch links make the first ping fail). Raw output is included only for failures. The standard way to
verify a CCNA lab end to end.

Examples:
- "Can PC1 reach its gateway, the server and the other LAN?"
- "Verify connectivity from PC1 to 192.168.1.1, 192.168.2.10 and 8.8.8.8"
- "Is my static routing working?"

source.description: Device display name as shown in Packet Tracer (e.g. 'Router0', 'PC1')

destinations.description: IP addresses or hostnames to ping

attempts.description: Pings per destination if all packets are lost

output.description: Raw ping output (only included on failure)

name: get_console_log
title: Get Console Log for a Device
description:
Return the device's console/terminal buffer as shown in its CLI tab (or the PC's Command Prompt):
boot messages, %LINK/%LINEPROTO and other syslog messages, and recent command output.

Examples:
- "Show R1's console messages"
- "Did any interface go down on the switch?"
- "What happened on PC1's command prompt?"

name.description: Device display name as shown in Packet Tracer (e.g. 'Router0', 'PC1')

max_chars.description: Return at most this many trailing characters

annotations.title: Get Console Log for a Device

name: get_command_history
title: Get Command History
description:
Return Packet Tracer's command log: commands typed into device terminals (by a person in the CLI tab, or by
send_terminal_command/verify_connectivity; send_cli_command and configure_device are not logged), with time,
device and prompt
(so the mode is visible, e.g. "R1(config-if)#"). Great for reviewing how a lab was solved, spotting a
typo, or building a study sheet of the commands used. Most recent last.

Examples:
- "What commands did I type on R1?"
- "Make me a cheat sheet from the commands I used in this lab"
- "Which command did I mistype?"

name.description: Only this device (display name); omit for all devices

name: get_device_configuration
title: Get a Device's Configuration
description:
Return a Cisco device's running-config (default) or startup-config as text. Useful for reviewing
a lab, comparing running vs startup ("did I save?"), or exporting a config to reuse.

Examples:
- "Show me R1's running config"
- "Is SW1's startup config the same as its running config?"

name.description: Device display name as shown in Packet Tracer (e.g. 'Router0', 'PC1')

name: configure_device
title: Configure a Cisco Device
description:
Apply a block of IOS configuration to a Cisco device, like pasting it into the CLI in global
config mode. Accepts output of `show running-config` as-is: "!" lines, "end", "enable",
"configure terminal", "version", and prompt lines are skipped. Indentation does not matter.
Returns how many commands were sent and only the ones IOS rejected. save=true runs
"write memory" afterwards.

Prefer this over send_cli_command for multi-line configs (VLANs, OSPF, ACLs, interface blocks).

CRITICAL: Changes device configuration. Show the user the config and confirm before applying.

Examples:
- "Configure OSPF area 0 on R1 for 10.0.0.0/8"
- "Apply this config to SW1 and save it"
- "Create VLANs 10 and 20 on the switch and assign Fa0/1-12 to VLAN 10"

name.description: Device display name as shown in Packet Tracer (e.g. 'Router0', 'PC1')

status.description: ok | rejected (IOS printed a '% ...' error) | ambiguous | invalid | incomplete | not_implemented

name: save_device_configuration
title: Save a Device's Configuration
description:
Save a Cisco device's running-config to startup-config ("write memory" / "copy run start") so it
survives a reload or power cycle. Returns true when IOS reports [OK].

Examples:
- "Save R1's config"
- "Make sure all my changes on SW1 survive a reload"

name.description: Device display name as shown in Packet Tracer (e.g. 'Router0', 'PC1')

name: erase_device_configuration
title: Erase a Device's Configuration
description:
Erase a Cisco device's startup-config ("write erase") and, by default, reload it so it boots with a
blank configuration -- the classic way to reset lab gear. Prompts are answered automatically
(the running config is NOT saved before reload).

CRITICAL: Destructive and irreversible. Always ask "Erase the configuration of [device]?" and wait
for the user's "yes" before invoking this tool.

Examples:
- "Wipe R1's configuration"
- "Reset the switch to factory defaults"

name.description: Device display name as shown in Packet Tracer (e.g. 'Router0', 'PC1')

status.description: ok | rejected (IOS printed a '% ...' error) | ambiguous | invalid | incomplete | not_implemented

name: get_device_model_details
title: Get Device Model Details (Slots and Modules)
description:
Show a device's expansion slots (installed module and its ports, or empty) and every module model it
supports with Packet Tracer's description. Use before add_module_to_device.

Examples:
- "What modules can I add to R1?"
- "Which slots on the 2911 are free?"
- "Does this router have serial interfaces?"

name.description: Device display name as shown in Packet Tracer (e.g. 'Router0', 'PC1')

slot.description: Slot path used by add_module_to_device, e.g. '0/0'

module.description: Installed module model, or null if the slot is empty

annotations.title: Get Device Model Details (Slots and Modules)

name: add_module_to_device
title: Add a Module to a Device
description:
Install a hardware module (e.g. HWIC-2T for two serial ports, NIM-2T on ISR4000s, HWIC-4ESW, SFPs)
into a free slot. The device is powered off for the change and powered back on, so an unsaved
running-config on it is lost -- save first if needed. Returns the new port names
(e.g. ["Serial0/0/0", "Serial0/0/1"]).

Examples:
- "Add a serial card to R1 so I can do a WAN link"
- "Put an HWIC-2T in slot 0/0 of R2"
- "Add a NIM-2T to the ISR4331"

name.description: Device display name as shown in Packet Tracer (e.g. 'Router0', 'PC1')

annotations.title: Add a Module to a Device

name: remove_module_from_device
title: Remove a Module from a Device
description:
Remove the module in a slot. The device is power-cycled; cables on the module's ports are removed.

CRITICAL: Destructive. Confirm with the user ("Remove the module in [slot] of [device]?") first.

Examples:
- "Take the serial card out of R1 slot 0/0"

name.description: Device display name as shown in Packet Tracer (e.g. 'Router0', 'PC1')

annotations.title: Remove a Module from a Device

name: create_full_network_topology
title: Create a Full Network Topology
description:
Build a whole network in one call into the open Packet Tracer file (existing devices are kept).
Same format export_network_topology returns, so exports can be rebuilt. Steps run in order:
devices (+modules), links, host IP settings, then IOS configs; errors are collected, not fatal.

Format:
{
  "description": "OSPF lab",
  "devices": [
    {"name": "R1", "device_type": "router", "model": "2911", "x": 100, "y": 100,
     "modules": [{"slot": "0/0", "module": "HWIC-2T"}],
     "config": "hostname R1\ninterface Gi0/0\n ip address 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.0\n no shutdown"},
    {"name": "SW1", "device_type": "switch", "model": "2960-24TT", "x": 300, "y": 100},
    {"name": "PC1", "device_type": "pc", "model": "PC-PT", "x": 500, "y": 100}
  ],
  "links": [{"device_a": "R1", "port_a": "GigabitEthernet0/0", "device_b": "SW1", "port_b": "GigabitEthernet0/1"},
            {"device_a": "PC1", "port_a": "FastEthernet0", "device_b": "SW1", "port_b": "FastEthernet0/1"}],
  "hosts": [{"name": "PC1", "port": "FastEthernet0", "ip_address": "192.168.1.10",
             "subnet_mask": "255.255.255.0", "default_gateway": "192.168.1.1"}]
}
Use full port names. cable defaults to "auto". Discover models with get_device_models and modules with
get_device_model_details.

Examples:
- "Build a 3-router OSPF lab with a LAN behind each router"
- "Recreate the topology I exported earlier"
- "Set up a router-on-a-stick lab with two VLANs"

description.description: Network description (Packet Tracer's File > Network description)

topology.description: Topology object (or its JSON string): description, devices, links, hosts -- see the docstring

name: export_network_topology
title: Export the Network Topology
description:
Export the open network as a topology object: devices (type, model, position, installed modules,
running-config), links, and host IPv4 settings. The result can be fed back to
create_full_network_topology, saved as a study reference, or reviewed for mistakes.

Examples:
- "Export my lab"
- "Give me a summary of everything in this network including configs"
- "Back up this topology as JSON"

description.description: Network description (Packet Tracer's File > Network description)

name: set_network_description
title: Set the Network Description
description:
Set the network file's description (shown in Packet Tracer under File > Network description / Info).
Handy for lab notes, objectives, or an IP addressing table.

Examples:
- "Describe this lab as 'CCNA 2 - OSPF single area practice'"
- "Put the addressing table in the network description"

name: get_annotations
title: Get Workspace Annotations
description:
List the notes and drawn shapes on the logical workspace with their ids, positions and note text.

Examples:
- "What notes are on my topology?"
- "Find the label that says 'LAN A'"

name: add_text_note
title: Add a Text Note
description:
Place a text note on the logical workspace (the "Place Note" tool) -- e.g. subnet labels,
"VLAN 10 - Sales", an addressing table, or lab instructions. Returns the note's id.

Examples:
- "Label the LAN behind R1 as 192.168.1.0/24"
- "Add a note with the lab objectives at the top"

name: add_line_annotation
title: Add a Line Annotation
description:
Draw a line on the logical workspace, e.g. to separate sites, mark a WAN boundary, or underline a label.
Returns the line's id.

Examples:
- "Draw a red line between the HQ and branch halves of the topology"
- "Underline the title note"

name: add_circle_annotation
title: Add a Circle Annotation
description:
Draw a circle on the logical workspace, e.g. to group a LAN, mark a broadcast or collision domain, or
highlight an OSPF area. Returns the circle's id (get_annotations lists circles as kind "ellipse").

Examples:
- "Circle the devices in VLAN 10"
- "Mark each broadcast domain with a circle"

name: edit_text_note
title: Edit a Text Note
description:
Replace the text of an existing note.

Examples:
- "Change the R1 LAN label to 10.1.1.0/24"

name: delete_annotation
title: Delete an Annotation
description:
Delete a note or drawn shape from the workspace.

CRITICAL: Destructive. Confirm with the user before deleting.

Examples:
- "Remove the old 'TODO' note"

name: set_simulation_mode
title: Switch Realtime/Simulation Mode
description:
Switch Packet Tracer between Simulation mode (enabled=true: time advances only when stepped, every packet
is recorded) and Realtime mode (enabled=false). Returns the resulting mode. Switching back to Realtime
clears the event list, so read events/details first.

Examples:
- "Switch to simulation mode so I can watch the ping"
- "Go back to realtime"

name: send_simple_pdu
title: Send a Simple PDU (ICMP)
description:
Create a Simple PDU (the envelope tool: an ICMP echo) from one device to another. In Simulation mode,
step_simulation then moves it hop by hop and get_simulation_events shows where it went -- including any
ARP it triggers. Returns the PDU's index in the user-created PDU list.

Examples:
- "Send a ping PDU from PC1 to the server and watch it"
- "Show me how ARP works between PC1 and R1"

source.description: Device display name as shown in Packet Tracer (e.g. 'Router0', 'PC1')

destination.description: Device display name as shown in Packet Tracer (e.g. 'Router0', 'PC1')

name: step_simulation
title: Step the Simulation
description:
Advance (or rewind) Simulation mode by N steps, like clicking Capture/Forward. Returns the simulation
time, total event count and how many new events were recorded.

Examples:
- "Step the simulation forward 5 times"
- "Go back one step"

name: get_simulation_events
title: Get Simulation Events
description:
List Simulation-mode events (the Event List): time, the device the PDU is at, where it came from,
protocol, and what happened (sent, accepted, dropped, buffered...).

Examples:
- "Where did the ping go?"
- "Show only the ARP events"
- "Did any packet get dropped?"

protocol.description: Only this protocol, e.g. ICMP, ARP, OSPF, STP, DHCP
Traffic type label, e.g. ICMP, ARP, OSPF, STP

status.description: sent | accepted | dropped | buffered | collided | in_transit | not_forwarded | unexpected

name: get_simulation_event_details
title: Get Simulation Event Details
description:
Explain one Simulation-mode event the way Packet Tracer's PDU Information window does: the device's
OSI-layer decisions in plain English ("The frame destination MAC address is not in the MAC table. The
Switch floods the frame...") plus the inbound and outbound headers decoded field by field (Ethernet,
802.1Q, IP, ICMP, ARP, TCP/UDP, STP, OSPF, DHCP, ...). Great for learning why a packet was forwarded or dropped.

Examples:
- "Why was event 2 dropped?"
- "What does the switch do with the frame at event 1?"
- "Show me the IP and Ethernet headers of the ping"

protocol.description: Traffic type label, e.g. ICMP, ARP, OSPF, STP

status.description: sent | accepted | dropped | buffered | collided | in_transit | not_forwarded | unexpected

decisions.description: Packet Tracer's OSI-layer explanation of what the device did

header.description: Header/PDU type, e.g. EthernetIIHeader, IpHeader, IcmpMessage
Header/PDU type, e.g. EthernetIIHeader, IpHeader, IcmpMessage

name: reset_simulation
title: Reset the Simulation
description:
Clear the Simulation-mode event list and restart simulation time (Reset Simulation). Device
configurations are not changed.

Examples:
- "Clear the event list"
- "Start the simulation over"

name: get_activity_instructions
title: Get Activity Instructions
description:
If the open file is a Packet Tracer activity (.pka, e.g. a NetAcad CCNA lab), return its instruction pages
as plain text: objectives, addressing table, and the tasks to complete.

This server cannot read an activity's answers, score or completion percentage (it does not hold Packet
Tracer's ACTIVITY_WIZARD privilege). Use Check Results in Packet Tracer for grading. When helping a
student, prefer explaining concepts and hinting over doing the graded tasks for them.

Examples:
- "What does this activity ask me to do?"
- "Read me the addressing table from the instructions"
- "Explain task 3 of this lab"

name: create_new_network
title: Create a New Empty Network
description:
Close the current network and start a new, empty one without a save prompt.

CRITICAL: Unsaved changes to the current network are lost. Always ask "Discard the current network?"
(or offer save_network_file first) and wait for the user's "yes" before invoking this tool.

Examples:
- "Start a fresh topology"
- "Clear the workspace"

name: open_network_file
title: Open a Network File
description:
Open a .pkt (network) or .pka (activity) file. Returns Packet Tracer's result code.

CRITICAL: Replaces the open network; unsaved changes may be lost. Confirm with the user first.

Examples:
- "Open ~/labs/ospf.pkt"
- "Load the activity file I downloaded"

path.description: Absolute path to a .pkt/.pka file on the Packet Tracer host

name: save_network_file
title: Save the Network to a File
description:
Save the current network as a .pkt file at an absolute path, without a dialog. Overwrites an
existing file at that path. Returns the saved path.

Examples:
- "Save this topology to ~/labs/campus.pkt"
- "Back up the network"

path.description: Absolute path to a .pkt/.pka file on the Packet Tracer host

annotations.title: Save the Network to a File

name: describe_ipc_class
title: Describe a Packet Tracer IPC Class
description:
Show an IPC class's inheritance and method signatures, (param types) -> return type plus the
ExApp privilege each needs. Use with call_ipc_api.

Examples:
- "What methods does a Router have for OSPF?" -> class_name="OspfProcess"
- "How do I read a port's MAC address?" -> class_name="Port", name_filter="mac"

class_name.description: IPC class, e.g. Router, CiscoDevice, HostPort, LogicalWorkspace, AppWindow

name_filter.description: Only methods whose name contains this text

annotations.title: Describe a Packet Tracer IPC Class
